text:
cami: quick heads-up — saw a user report in support about the console flagging a routing YAML as invalid even though it passes our schema. example snippet they pasted:

cami: ```yaml
route:
  match:
    - header:
        name: X-Account
        regex: ^acct_\d+$
  upstream: payments-service
  timeout_ms: 5000
```

cami: console shows a lint error: "header.matchers must be static string or exact match". that seems wrong since we explicitly allow regex. :thinking:

liam: hmm, we recently tightened the editor linter to reject complex regexes that use lookarounds because they break the runtime's matcher compiler. maybe the UX isn't surfacing the real reason though.

anya: do we have the list of supported regex features in the docs? support could point users there instead of a vague lint.

dinesh: the linter rule is `no_unsafe_regex` and it runs both in the console frontend and in CI. frontend currently does a quick heuristic: if pattern contains `(?` or `(?<=` it fails. but that heuristic is too aggressive — `^acct_\d+$` matches fine.

cami: right — customer has simple numeric capture, not lookbehind. their UX is confusing because it suggests the schema is wrong, not the heuristic.

infra-bot: deploy 2054.32 -> routing-lint-heuristics updated. CI: all checks passed.

liam: proposal: change linter message to include reason like "heuristic rejection: advanced regex features (lookarounds) may not compile on some kernels — see docs link" and add a "why?" tooltip in the console.

anya: +1. also add a quick autofix suggestion: "use simple character classes or anchors" with a copy-to-clipboard safe example.

dinesh: implementation note: keep the heuristic in frontend for quick feedback but mirror the exact same rule server-side so save/rollout still fails consistently. We should also add a unit test in `eng-platform/routing-linter` that enumerates supported regex syntax.

cami: UX question: if a user insists on the risky regex and chooses to bypass lint in the editor, do we allow save with a warning? current flow blocks save entirely.

liam: for dedicated/private customers with opt-in runtimes we allow force-save via an explicit checkbox + audit log. for hosted we should probably block by default unless they have an enterprise override.

anya: can we avoid a full block and instead show a red modal that requires the user to type "I understand" and logs the acknowledgment? gives traces for support.

dinesh: agree on modal. add telemetry event `routing_lint_override` that includes route id, user id, and rule id. send it to console telemetry with sampling 1% for public tiers and 100% for enterprise trials.

sre-jen: if we let users bypass, make sure rollout policies protect prod traffic — auto-fallback to stable variant if matchers cause runtime compile errors. Otherwise we'll get paging at 2am.

liam: noted. action items: 1) change linter message text (frontend) 2) add tooltip + docs link 3) implement modal + audit log for override 4) add server-side mirror + unit tests 5) telemetry event + sampling rules 6) rollout fallback guard. assigning: dinesh (1,4), anya (2,3), liam (5,6), cami to coordinate with support for the customer reply.

cami: thanks — i'll reply to the ticket with the interim workaround (use `^acct_\d+$` or ask for enterprise override) and track the PRs. :thumbsup:
